chapter: 6 — Measuring What Matters: From Telemetry to Architecture Decisions
evidence: 'With the canonical 9.2K KV re-read included, intensity saturates at ~6.8 FLOP/byte (164.1 GFLOP — 140 projection + 24.1 attention — ÷ 24.1 GB of canonical 9.2K FP16 KV; ~5.8 at batch 32), so decode stays bandwidth-bound at every batch size — Ch 8.'
issue: The denominator is not the same at the two displayed operating points. 164.1 ÷ 24.1 = 6.8 counts both the projection and attention FLOPs but divides by KV bytes only, silently dropping the 140 GB weight read that appears in the same sentence's numerator. The quoted ~5.8 at batch 32 is obtained only if weight bytes are included: 32 × 164.1 = 5251.2 GFLOP ÷ (32 × 24.1 + 140) = 911.2 GB = 5.76 ≈ 5.8. A consistent batch-1 combined intensity is 164.1 ÷ (140 + 24.1) ≈ 1.0 FLOP/byte, not 6.8. Separately, 'saturates' contradicts the displayed decline from 6.8 to 5.8. The bandwidth-bound conclusion may still hold (both values are far below the ridge ~295), but the displayed arithmetic does not support the stated numbers.
fix_instruction: State one denominator rule and apply it at both points: if weight bytes are counted when weights appear in the numerator, batch 1 is ~1.0 FLOP/byte and batch 32 is ~5.8 FLOP/byte. Remove 'saturates' or show a monotonic curve with its formula, and reconcile the wording with the Ch. 8 roofline treatment.
